news.title: 2014 World Cup top scorer James Rodriguez has retired from the Colombian national team
news.lede: James Rodriguez, the 2014 World Cup's top scorer, has retired from the Colombian national team, the player announced this on his Instagram page, APA reports. "Thank you for every game, every joy, every tear, and every shared happiness. Defending the colors of the Colombian national team is one of the greatest honors of my life," Rodriguez wrote.

news.title: 'It was the moment' - Tuchel reveals bizarre World Cup regret
news.lede: The Three Lions’ 3-2 victory over the co-hosts in July was one of the tournament’s most enthralling matches. Two goals from Jude Bellingham and a Harry Kane penalty was enough for ten-man England to see off a second-half Mexican onslaught. The win was made all the more impressive due to the match being played 2,240 metres above sea level – a condition that Tuchel's men were not physically conditioned for. The German sat down with Daniel Sturridge in ‘Reflections: England’s World Cup Journey’ - to be released on Wednesday - to reflect on the eventful night in Mexico City and revealed his one regret, albeit a slightly bizarre one.

news.title: From Segura to Maltby: six breakout stars from the Women’s Under-20 World Cup
news.lede: With an incredible array of talent on show we select half a dozen players who could make the step up to the senior World Cup next year. The 2026 Under-20 Women’s World Cup is entering the knockout stage in Poland and, after an intriguing group stage, we pick some of the young stars who have stood out. Celia Segura (Spain and Barcelona) Segura is no stranger to knockout football, having helped Spain to silver at the Under-17 World Cup two years ago and finishing with the Bronze Ball and Bronze Boot. She has picked up the mantle again as La Roja eased through their group.

news.title: Thomas Tuchel: England boss regrets not eating Azteca turf after World Cup win in Mexico
news.lede: Tuchel led England to the semi-finals in his first major tournament in charge. Thomas Tuchel regrets not eating any of the grass at the Azteca Stadium after England's World Cup win against Mexico. His Three Lions beat the co-hosts 3-2 in the last-16 tie in July, despite playing much of the second half with 10 men following Jarell Quansah's red card. England went on to reach the semi-finals, where they lost to Argentina, before beating France in the Bronze medal match for third place.

news.title: 'Get ready for one of the best experiences in college football':…
news.lede: The German World Cup fan who went viral for his six-week tour of North America, including Alabama, is making a swift return to Jordan-Hare Stadium to watch Auburn host the Florida Gators this weekend. Freddy from Germany watched a World Cup friendly in June at Jordan-Hare Stadium, saying that the European mind could not "comprehend" the SEC football atmosphere he was treated to. He amassed over 750,000 followers on Twitter as he journaled his trip around the United States and Canada. news.title: 2014 World Cup star James Rodriguez retires from national team
news.lede: Colombian football star James Rodriguez, one of the best players in the country's history, on Tuesday announced his retirement from the national team after 15 years and three World Cups. "I'm leaving with serenity because I know I gave absolutely everything," the 35-year-old captain said in a social media video, his eyes welling with tears. Rodriguez powered himself and his country to stardom at the 2014 World Cup in Brazil, when Los Cafeteros made the quarterfinals for the first time. He won the tournament's Golden Boot as the top scorer and became a global superstar.
